title: Positive roots have simple-root words with root partial sums
statement:
Let $I$ be finite and let $M,N$ be $\mathbf Q$-vector spaces over the rational field [def-weil-field]. Let $P:\operatorname{RootPairing}\ I\ \mathbf Q\ M\ N$ be a crystallographic root pairing: its root and coroot families $a_i\in M$, $c_i\in N$ are injective, have a perfect bilinear pairing with $\langle a_i,c_i\rangle=2$, have integral mutual pairings, and the two root reflections permute the families with the same permutation. Let $b:P.\operatorname{Base}$ have support $D\subseteq I$: the root and coroot families on $D$ are linearly independent, and each root and each coroot or its negative is a nonnegative integer sum of its corresponding family on $D$. A root $a_i$ is positive if it is a nonnegative integer sum of $(a_j)_{j\in D}$. For every positive root $a_i$ there exist $n\in\mathbf N$ and a sequence $j_0,\ldots,j_{n-1}\in D$ such that
$$a_i=\sum_{m=0}^{n-1}a_{j_m},\qquad \sum_{m=0}^k a_{j_m}\in\{a_j:j\in I\}\quad(0\le k<n).$$
Here a nonnegative integer sum includes the empty sum.

mathlib_match.how: Exact specialization to Q at lines 609--624. The output f : Fin n -> I is the stated sequence, range f lies in b.support, and every sum over m <= k is a root. IsPos is equivalent to being a nonnegative integer sum, because Base coordinates are sign-coherent and roots are nonzero (the height is the sum of these coordinates).
